title: A dynamic machine learning model for prediction of NAFLD in a health checkup population: A longitudinal study.
summary: An LSTM updated with successive health-check records predicted later NAFLD in retrospective cohorts, with AUROC .818 internally and .792 externally after five checkups; this does not show prospective clinical benefit. The study does not establish external generalization, causal effects or sustained operational impact.
ai_technology: LSTM consumes successively updated records; L1-penalized logistic regression selected features and SHAP explained predictions.
organization: Chongqing Research Institute of Big Data, Peking University, Chongqing, China

evidence.tested: In 10,493 retrospective participants, internal AUROC rose .729 to .818; external cohort of 1,728 had .700 to .792.
evidence.unknown: Training-set five-fold tuning and separate internal/external validation assessed discrimination and calibration; no prospective deployment or clinical benefit was tested.
evidence.ai_role: LSTM consumes successively updated records; L1-penalized logistic regression selected features and SHAP explained predictions.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
